summary.headline: Artemis FY26 revenue rose 15.4% to INR 1,081 crore and Q4 EBITDA margin reached 21.3%, with Raipur losses of INR 18-20 crore guided for FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR 1,081 crore (+15.4% YoY), EBITDA INR 218 crore (20.2% margin) and PAT INR 104 crore (+26.2%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 279 crore (+16.4%), EBITDA INR 59 crore (21.3% margin) and PAT INR 30 crore (+32.1%). Management said international patient volumes fell 15-18% in March on the West Asia conflict but had recovered to about 90% by mid-May. Management expects FY27 growth from Gurgaon bed additions and the Raipur hospital, which will dilute EBITDA margin by about 1-1.5% in the near term.

segments.name: Gurgaon flagship
segments.commentary: Occupancy 64.6% in Q4 and ARPOB up 7.3% YoY to INR 84,571. Management says Gurgaon EBITDA margin is 21.2% (19.4% excluding other income) and guides to above 20% going forward.

segments.name: International patients
segments.commentary: Grew 26.9% in FY26 and is about 30-31% of revenue; ARPOB is about 1.3x domestic. Middle East is about 30% of international patients, with growth in Africa and CIS and new markets in West Africa, Canada and the Nordics.

segments.name: Mauritius hospitals
segments.commentary: First hospital has broken even and is profitable; second hospital started in April 2026, and bed capacity is rising from 80 to 110.

segments.name: Raipur (300 beds)
segments.commentary: Opens Q1 FY27 with 150 beds, adding 50 more within 3-4 months. Expected FY27 revenue INR 80-85 crore with a loss of INR 18-20 crore; breakeven in about 18 months. Capex INR 110-120 crore.

segments.name: Daffodil and cardiac care units
segments.commentary: Management says these are at EBITDA breakeven and making small profits.

guidance_outlook: Gurgaon revenue to grow 15-17% YoY; at least 30% of incremental revenue to flow to EBITDA over 3-4 years.
Raipur losses of INR 18-20 crore in FY27 to dilute consolidated EBITDA margin by about 1-1.5% for roughly 15 months, then turn accretive after breakeven.
Targeting 2,000 beds by 2029 from about 800 now; Gurgaon operational beds to rise by 50 twice once occupancy holds at 70% for a quarter, with 70% occupancy targeted by Q2 FY27.
FY27 budget assumes at least 15% growth in top line: 15% domestic and 15% international, with a 70:30 domestic-to-international mix.
Pricing: insurer contracts lock prices for three years, so effective price increase is about 3% a year; ARPOB growth to come mainly from case mix and efficiency.

Net debt peak could reach about INR 350 crore (currently about INR 260 crore); INR 700 crore fundraise approved by board, pending shareholder approval, mainly for deposits on new brownfield or greenfield projects.
capex_capacity: South Delhi 650-bed facility: about INR 500 crore total (450 beds for about INR 350 crore, 200 beds for INR 150-160 crore), about INR 75-80 lakh per bed for Artemis's interiors and equipment; land and building owned by the trust. Two phases, with commissioning planned in FY29 and Artemis capex mainly from mid-FY28.
Raipur 300-bed hospital: capex INR 110-120 crore; about 50-60% already spent; remaining INR 50-60 crore. Total FY27 capex about INR 100 crore including Gurgaon replacement capex.

Gurgaon: Platinum Green Building certification gives 15% additional FAR, enabling about 100 extra beds; decision on starting these in FY27 or taking another brownfield/greenfield project expected within weeks.
Gurgaon operational beds were 544 on average in FY26 (546 cited); Raipur adds 200 beds in FY27 for 300 in total.
demand_pricing: International patient volumes fell 15-18% in March 2026 due to the West Asia conflict; management says they had recovered to about 90% by mid-May.
High-end surgery volumes (neuro, cardiac, onco, transplants) are rising in both domestic and international segments, partly offsetting the March dip.
Oncology case mix dipped slightly because TPAs pushed back on immunotherapy and government chemotherapy payments were paused; management says both are now resolved.

Management says Artemis is priced slightly below large competitors; the price increase is about 3-5% a year, ending near 3% after insurer lock-ins. Says it is at the Medanta level and below Fortis and Max.
Raipur ARPOB assumed at INR 33,000-35,000 to start, rising with transplants and high-end services; management cites lower operating costs in Tier-2 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gurgaon EBITDA margin hold at about 21% and how will Raipur losses affect blended margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would be maintained or improved; Raipur losses of INR 18-20 crore would reduce consolidated EBITDA margin by about 1-1.5% in the first year, with recovery after breakeven in about 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company raising INR 700 crore when internal accruals and debt appear sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt for Raipur and South Delhi may reach about INR 350 crore (currently about INR 260 crore). The raise is for deposits on new brownfield or greenfield projects that cannot be debt-funded; one or two projects are to be finalised in four to six weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the return threshold for new capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 16-18% ROCE within three to five years on new capital, with payback within five to six years; current ROCE is about 14.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Raipur market outlook and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees Raipur as a nodal centre for Chhattisgarh, where about 60% of patients currently travel to Mumbai or Delhi. Competitors entering include Manipal and Lilavati, and Artemis cites a first-mover advantage and a PWC market survey.

qa_highlights.question: Will Gurgaon occupancy exceed 70%, and when will extra beds open?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy is 64.6%; management expects to reach 70% or more by Q2 FY27, and 50 beds will open after a quarter at 70%, with another 50 after that.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EWS obligation?
qa_highlights.answer: EWS is 20% in Gurgaon, 10% in Delhi and likely below 10% in Raipur; management says compliance has been without issues for 18-19 years.

risks_watch: Raipur ramp-up: INR 18-20 crore FY27 loss and breakeven in about 15-18 months; doctor onboarding starts in June 2026.
Geopolitical exposure: international patients fell 15-18% in March 2026; recovery to about 90% is not yet fully confirmed.
Government medical-device margin cap under discussion; management says there is no notification yet.
Capital deployment: INR 700 crore raise needs shareholder approval; new projects not yet named; peak debt may reach about INR 350 crore.
Operating cash flow conversion questioned on the call; management said FY26 CFO was about 60% of EBITDA, but could not confirm the YoY comparison and offered to follow up offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and Gurgaon margins, with specific numbers on beds, capex and Raipur losses. Cautious and sometimes evasive on the Delhi/Raipur guidance, the INR 700 crore raise, and cash flow, where management deferred to offline follow-up.
